summary: Well-executed, fully preregistered paired confirmatory run comparing LLM-only generation to a GVR pipeline for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Execution artifacts, per-episode hashes, and analysis are thoroughly archived. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms) produced identical outputs across arms for all 200 confirmatory tasks, yielding a degenerate null result (200/200 verifier-accepted in both arms). The study is reproducible and transparent, but manuscript clarifications are required to avoid misinterpretation of the confirmatory null and to disclose a post-hoc test choice rationale.
critical_issues: The preregistered analysis plan specified use of the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for the primary paired analysis on the binary operational-failure indicator, but the reported confirmatory inference uses an exact McNemar test (appropriate for paired binary outcomes). The manuscript does not label this as a post-preregistration deviation or justify the change.

The preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation_semantics produced identical LLM outputs under both arms for every confirmatory task (repair_attempts = 0), which mechanically prevents the preregistered primary test from detecting any repair-driven effect. While the manuscript discusses this in the body, the presentation risks being read as a substantive null result rather than a boundary-conditional null; that risk must be removed by clearer, prominent statements.

Power-plan assumptions were violated in practice because the observed baseline failure rate was 0%, invalidating the preregistered power target and reducing inferential informativeness. This is acknowledged in the limitations but must be made explicit in the abstract and contribution statements so readers cannot overinterpret the null.
required_revisions: Explicitly disclose in the manuscript (and in the preregistration/deviations section) that the originally preregistered Wilcoxon signed-rank test was not used for the primary binary contingency and that an exact paired-contingency test (McNemar) was applied instead; state a clear, concise justification referencing the binary/degenerate contingency structure and cite the archived contingency counts and analysis artifact (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 7bc1bd2a...).

Add a compact, prominent expedition (one-paragraph) in the Abstract and in the Introduction/Contributions that states the shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM call per task) produced identical baseline and guarded candidates for all confirmatory tasks (n=200), that repair_attempts = 0, and that therefore the primary paired test is boundary-conditional (i.e., mechanically uninformative about repair value under independent-generation sampling). Reference the execution_manifest and representative artifact hashes (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA-256 f8de4d6e..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA-256 9235bce7...) to support the statement.

Include a short, machine-verifiable summary table or sentence in Results showing model_calls_used = 200 (one model call per confirmatory task) versus planned maximum_model_calls = 400, and the per-task equality evidence (e.g., proportion of confirmatory pairs with identical response-hash across baseline and guarded; show the hash-equality count and point to the response-file listing in execution_manifest).

Amend the Threats-to-Validity / Limitations section to more explicitly state that the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline failure; report that baseline success = 100% in confirmatory bank and explain the consequence for confirmatory inference (i.e., the primary test could not detect the preregistered MDE). Cross-reference the preregistration power-plan and the observed contingency.

Add an explicit 'Deviations from Preregistration' entry in the manuscript that lists (a) the choice to implement shared_initial_candidate (if not already flagged as a deviation), (b) the analytical test selection change (Wilcoxon → McNemar) and justification, and (c) any other minor bookkeeping or reporting differences; reference the archived preregistration JSON and execution_manifest hashes so readers can verify.
optional_revisions: Include one or two representative example configurations (baseline/guarded) as short appendix snippets or figure in the main paper (ensuring page limit) to make the equality observation concrete for readers; cite the response-file paths and hashes.

Discuss briefly—within the existing limitations/discussion text—likely experimental modifications (independent-generation, per-arm sampling, multiple stochastic seeds or multiple models) and point to the archived artifacts needed to reproduce such follow-ups, to help future researchers build on this run.

State more explicitly in the Discussion what practical scenarios remain where GVR is expected to show real benefit (e.g., non-deterministic generation, heterogeneous firmware), to avoid readers misinterpreting the result as broad evidence against GVR.
